meta.title: Historia-globen – see what happened at the same time around the world
meta.description: Explore world history on a spinning globe. Drag through time and see what happened at the same time in different parts of the world.

help.title: How to use the globe
help.s1t: Spin it with your finger or the mouse. Pinch or scroll to zoom.
help.s2t: Tap the year or drag the timeline.
help.s3t: Choose a war, an empire or a religion under Search and follow.
help.m1: All events have the same brass medal. The symbol and the inner colour show the category.
help.m2: The arc under the medal is a small timeline. The whole arc: ongoing in the year you are at. Left part: has already happened. Right part: comes later. The arc shows when you zoom in.
help.m4: Dashed arc: uncertain information (approximate year or sources that differ).
help.m5: Cluster: the number is the number of events, and the colours of the ring show the categories. With the mouse pointer over the cluster, or when you go to it with Tab, you see what it contains, for example “3 war events, 2 empires and civilisations”.
help.m6: Religions (in Layers): the symbol in an area and next to the colour shows the religion, for example a cross for Christianity. A medal with the symbol stands where the religion arose. It appears in the year the religion arose and stays as long as the religion layer is on. Click it to read about the religion. Point at a religion in the lists or in the legend to highlight it on the map.
help.m7: Empires: a medal in the middle of an empire shows its symbol, for example the eagle for Rome. Point at it to see the name and click it to read about the empire. When you zoom in, the name stands under the symbol.

sources.title: About the sources
sources.urval.title: About the selection
sources.urval.p1: The globe shows a selection, not everything that has happened. The selection is made by one person who created the site as a hobby project, without an editorial team.
sources.urval.p2: Something being included is not a statement of opinion. The site does not take a side on political or disputed questions. Where a border or status is disputed, the map follows Sweden's official position, with a source for each case.
sources.urval.p3: What is included should be documented in an open source and be significant according to established reference works. Ideally it also shows an unexpected connection, fills a gap in time or place, or belongs to school subjects.
sources.urval.p4: Some parts of the world and some periods are still thinner than others. This is being evened out over time.
sources.urval.p5: Missing something, or found a mistake? Use "Report a factual error" in the fact box or "Send a suggestion" in Help. Suggestions are welcome, but the site's creator decides what is included.

focus.note.empires: Borders from Cliopatria. The years show when map data exists and can differ from the empire's historical years. A colonial empire has the same colour everywhere; the star and the heavy border show the home country. A soft, blurred edge means that the sources say the boundary is uncertain. Sparse dots with a dashed border are influence: tributaries and vassals according to Cliopatria. Countries that no longer exist are listed under Vanished countries.
focus.note.vanished: Countries that no longer exist: when they were formed and dissolved according to the sources, and which countries they became. Borders from Cliopatria, which can have other years.
focus.note.religions: Shows where the religion was the official or main religion of a state, not the age of the religion or where all believers lived.
focus.note.routes: Follow a journey at its own pace. There are pauses only at places with dates supported by sources.

sources.policy1: Each claim has at least one source, with a link and the date it was checked.
sources.policy2: Each claim has a review status: draft, source-checked, or two sources agree. Drafts are not shown.
sources.policy3: “Two sources agree” means the year and place have been compared with a second, independent source, such as Wikidata, and agree.
sources.policy4: Claims suggested by Claude are drafts until the source has been opened and checked.
sources.policy5: Uncertainty is shown openly, such as “around” or a range. Disagreements between sources are noted in the fact box.
sources.policy6: A fun fact comparing two things has a source for both.
